facts.authoredFrom: Read from the case's input bytes: grund.toml (version 1, project_name "fixture", strict, `require_grounding = false`, `[id] format = "{kind}-{slug}"`, one untitled FS kind on the folder docs/fs with `index = false`, and no `[scan]` table, so the default include reads docs and src with the default extensions and the default comment prefixes, `/*` among them, §FS-config.3.5); the FS home docs/fs does not exist and scans as nothing with no finding (§FS-scan.scope.homes); src/lib.rs line 1 is the one-line Javadoc `/** FS-b: Beta */` above the code line `pub struct B;`. That opener line is in declaration position (§FS-declarations.line.block-comment), so it declares FS-b at line 1 with a null anchor (§FS-show.3.1.3.1); the `*/` closing the comment on the heading's own line is comment envelope, not part of the title (§FS-languages.comment-wrapper.headings), so the title is Beta and the editor's title span `FS-b: Beta` ends before it (§FS-lsp.1.3.4). The block closes on its own line, so it is that line alone and line 2 is outside it (§FS-languages.comment-block.close): the body under the heading is empty, with no section. docs/use.md carries one line, `See §FS-b.`, a marked citation under no heading, so outside any declaration; it resolves to the source declaration, which is therefore cited. Every citation resolves and the one declaration is cited, so the only finding is the site-less version caution (§FS-check.2.1.1). Cross-reference emission wraps that citation as a link to src/lib.rs, relative to docs/, with no anchor because the target's home is a source file (§FS-fmt.6.2, §FS-show.3.1.3.1); the Rust file is not Markdown and is never rewritten (§FS-fmt.6.1). FS-absent is the absent control, an ID of the config's format that nothing declares or cites.

findings.message: grund.toml is version 1; migrate it with grund config migrate --to 2
